discovery: Theory of quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computation, including topological (surface/toric) codes
subfield: Quantum information physics / quantum error correction
motivation: Before 1995 it was widely believed that decoherence makes large-scale quantum coherence fundamentally unprotectable, since quantum states cannot be copied or measured without disturbance. Shor and, independently, Steane discovered that quantum information can be encoded redundantly in entangled states so that errors are detected through syndrome measurements and corrected without learning the encoded state. Kitaev then showed that topologically ordered systems, the toric and surface codes, store quantum information non-locally with only local check measurements and an error threshold, the architecture now used in leading experiments. These ideas revealed a new physical principle: entanglement can actively stabilize quantum states against noise. In the past few years experiments on superconducting circuits, trapped ions and neutral atoms have realized repeated error correction and logical qubits whose errors fall as code distance increases, below threshold. The theory has become the foundation of a new regime of controllable quantum matter.
